content.title: Is Worrying About Tomorrow Keeping You Awake Today?
content.subtitle: Listen to an incredible story about Rizq.
content.body:
The dark prison of Kufa. Imam Ali ibn Asim al-Kufi, a distinguished hadith scholar and beloved student of Shaqiq al-Balkhi, the teacher of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, was imprisoned on false charges of treason. Sitting alone in his confined cell, the young scholar could not sleep. His mind was consumed by thoughts of his family going hungry. “I am chained behind iron bars. Who will put food into my little children’s mouths tomorrow morning? Who will care for my ailing wife?” The uncertainty and fear of the future left his heart feeling painfully empty.

Just then, his teacher, Shaqiq al-Balkhi, arrived. Seeing the intense anxiety on his student’s face, he gently asked, “What is troubling you so deeply?” The student burst into tears. “My teacher, I am trapped within these four walls. Who will provide sustenance for my children tomorrow in my absence?”

Shaqiq al-Balkhi smiled gently and shared a story that would become a source of comfort not only for that young man but also for anxious believers across generations.

The Blind Bird in the Desert and Its Unusual Sustenance

Shaqiq said, “Once, while travelling with a distant trade caravan, I stopped to rest in a desolate, waterless wilderness. There were no settlements around, not even a trace of greenery. Suddenly, I noticed a blind bird lying on the ground with a broken wing. It could neither fly nor see. I wondered, ‘How is this helpless bird surviving in this harsh desert? Who provides its food?’

Curious, I watched the bird from a hidden spot. A little while later, I witnessed something extraordinary! Another healthy bird flew in from a distance, carrying a small grasshopper in its beak. It landed beside the blind, injured bird and gently placed the food into its mouth.

Standing alone in the desert, I began to weep. The Lord who does not let a blind bird with a broken wing starve in the wilderness would surely not let His honoured creation, a human being with two functioning arms and legs, die of hunger. Impossible!”

Balancing the Means of Provision and Tawakkul

After hearing this story, tears of relief rolled down the cheeks of Imam Ali ibn Asim al-Kufi. He realised that we often rely so blindly on worldly means that we forget their Owner in an instant.

We believe our job provides our food and our business secures our children’s future. Yet a job or business is merely a means. Allah alone is the true Provider. When one means disappears, it does not mean the doors of sustenance have closed.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance He is truly due, He would provide for you just as He provides for the birds. They leave their nests hungry in the morning and return in the evening with full stomachs.”

(Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi: 2344)

Do Not Sacrifice Today’s Peace to Imaginary Disasters

A believer must work hard, giving their best in both physical and intellectual effort. But there is no need to carry the burden of the outcome on our own weak shoulders. You do not even know whether you will live to see the tomorrow that is keeping you awake tonight. Yet no power in the world can take away what Allah has destined for you.

Whenever an imagined crisis about the future threatens to overwhelm you in the silence of the night, remember the blind bird with the broken wing in the desert. Prostrate before Allah and say, “My Lord, I will do my best, but I entrust the responsibility for me and my family entirely to You.”

This unwavering trust in your Lord’s power will bring genuine peace of mind and a heavenly sense of comfort to your heart.

References and Bibliography:

  • Imam Abu Nu‘aym al-Isfahani, Hilyat al-Awliya wa Tabaqat al-Asfiya (حِلْيَةُ الأَوْلِيَاءِ وَطَبَقَاتُ الأَصْفِيَاءِ)

  • Imam Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidaya wa’l-Nihaya (البداية والنهاية)

  • Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, Sifat al-Safwa (صفة الصفوة)
